title: Court of Protection Paralegal

description:
Role: Court of Protection Paralegal (x 2 positions) - City of London

Leading law firm looking to recruit dedicated Court of Protection Paralegals for highly sought permanent positon.

Our client serves corporate entities and private individuals in over 25 practice areas from offices throughout London and across England and Wales. Our client holds the Investors in People Gold Accreditation Quality Standard Mark and is LEXCEL, Cyber Essentials Plus and ISO accredited and regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority.

Court of Protection Background:

Our client's Court of Protection finance team act as professional deputy, managing financial affairs for many vulnerable clients. Clients are referred by the Office of the Public Guardian to Philippa Barton as panel deputy, and by litigation teams acting for incapacitated clients who have recovered damages awards.

You will be responsible for day to day management of our clients' finances including building good relationships with clients, dealing with one off requests for payments, making applications to the court, managing building projects, managing tax and insurance issues and completing OPG reports.

The team also act for clients applying to be appointed as lay deputy and deal with probate matters.

The team director is ranked in Legal 500 and Chambers. Client testimonials say that the team is "knowledgeable about all things Court of Protection" and they are "empathetic, approachable and diligent."

The team is fast growing and very busy. The team works closely together and prioritises providing a high level of client care and a very efficient service.

Main Duties and Responsibilities
- Report directly to the Department Director.
- Assist solicitors and fee earners with the management of Court of Protection files from inception to conclusion.
- Support deputyship matters involving property and financial affairs and health and welfare issues.
- Prepare and draft Court of Protection applications, witness statements, court forms, and supporting documentation under supervision.
- Liaise with clients, family members, deputies, the Office of the Public Guardian, local authorities, healthcare professionals, and other third parties.
- Take client instructions and maintain regular communication with vulnerable clients and their representatives.
- Review and analyse medical records, mental capacity assessments, financial information, and other relevant evidence.
- Conduct legal research relating to the Mental Capacity Act 2005, Court of Protection practice and procedures, and related areas of law.
- Assist with the preparation of court bundles, hearing documentation, and correspondence.
- Attend meetings, conferences, and Court hearings where required.
- Maintain accurate file records and ensure compliance with internal procedures, regulatory obligations, and court deadlines.
- Record time accurately and assist the team in meeting departmental objectives.
- Implement feedback and recommendations from supervisors following file reviews.
- Deliver excellent client care with professionalism, empathy, patience, and sensitivity.

Key Skills Required
- Demonstrate passion and experience in a broad range of publicly funded Court of Protection matters
- A strong academic background with a Law degree
- Legal experience as a Court of Protection Paralegal/Advisor
- Clear understanding and application of Court of Protection
- Excellent communications skills to work effectively with all types of people
- Excellent written communication and drafting skills
- Excellent analytical and organisational skills and ability to use own initiative but know when to seek guidance
- Committed team player, self -motivated and professional
- Excellent IT Skills -familiar with Microsoft Office applications and document management skills
- Business acumen and the ability to market the Company.

On offer is an attractive salary package, a supportive team environment and real prospects for promotion. The Company will allow hybrid working.

Role: Personal Injury & Clinical Negligence Caseworker / Paralegal

Gemini Recruitment are delighted to be partnering with a large and established law firm that provides expert legal services to both corporate organisations and private individuals across more than 25 practice areas. With offices throughout London and across England and Wales, our client has built an exceptional reputation for delivering outstanding legal services and exceptional client care.

Recognised and recommended by The Legal 500 and Chambers and Partners, this top-tier firm is now seeking a Personal Injury & Clinical Negligence Caseworker to join its highly regarded Personal Injury and Clinical Negligence Department. This is an excellent opportunity for a motivated legal professional to develop their expertise within a supportive and collaborative environment, working alongside experienced practitioners on a varied and high-quality caseload.

Department Background:

The Personal Injury and Clinical Negligence Department acts on behalf of individuals who have suffered injury, illness, or loss as a result of accidents, medical negligence, and other incidents where compensation may be recoverable. The department is recognised for its client-focused approach, providing compassionate support while pursuing the best possible outcomes for clients throughout the claims process.

The team handles a broad range of complex and sensitive matters, including medical negligence claims, surgical errors, delayed or incorrect diagnoses, birth injury claims, road traffic accidents, workplace accidents, public liability claims, serious injury cases, and fatal accident claims. Working closely with clients, medical experts, and other professionals, the department is committed to delivering outstanding legal representation and achieving successful results.

Duties and responsibilities
- Report directly to the Department Director.
- Assist with a varied caseload of Personal Injury and Clinical Negligence matters.
- Attend clients, take instructions, and assist with case preparation.
- Draft correspondence, witness statements, and other legal documents.
- Prepare and organise evidence and supporting documentation.
- Liaise with clients, experts, counsel, insurers, and third parties.
- Attend conferences and court where required.
- Maintain accurate time recording and file management procedures.
- Ensure compliance with departmental and regulatory requirements.
- Deliver excellent client care with a professional and empathetic approach.

Experience and qualifications
- A strong academic background, including a Law degree or equivalent.
- Previous experience in Personal Injury and/or Clinical Negligence would be beneficial, along with an interest in these areas of law.
- Understanding of CPR, litigation procedures, and relevant pre-action protocols.
- Excellent client care, communication, and interpersonal skills.
- Strong organisational and analytical abilities.
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
- Excellent IT skills, including Microsoft Office and case management systems.
- Self-motivated, professional, and committed to delivering high standards of work.

Benefits
- Competitive salary package.
- Excellent career progression opportunities.
- Ongoing professional development and training.
- Support for relevant legal accreditations and professional recognition.
- Exposure to high-quality and diverse Personal Injury and Clinical Negligence work.
- Opportunity to work alongside highly experienced legal professionals.
- A supportive and collaborative team environment.

Company culture

Gemini Recruitment specialises in connecting exceptional legal professionals with some of the UK's most recognised and respected law firms. We are proud to partner with an award-winning, top-tier practice that is renowned for its supportive culture, commitment to employee development, and dedication to delivering outstanding client service.

The firm offers a welcoming and inclusive environment where individuals are valued, supported, and encouraged to progress their careers. With a strong emphasis on collaboration, professional excellence, and continuous learning, this is an excellent opportunity for an ambitious Personal Injury & Clinical Negligence Caseworker to join a leading legal practice and become part of a team committed to achieving the highest standards.

The recruitment process will fully comply with GDPR and all applicable employment legislation. Successful applicants may be subject to background screening, including DBS checks, to establish eligibility to work in the UK and suitability for the role.

title: Residential Property Paralegal
description:
Our client, an established law firm, is looking for a paralegal with solid experience in residential conveyancing to support a team of fee earners. Duties will include drafting and reviewing contracts, conducting title searches, communicating with clients, solicitors and third parties.

The successful candidate will have previous legal property experience and be familiar with preparing and submitting land registry forms and searches.

The successful candidate will have good IT literacy, be familiar with legal property work and be able to work as part of a team. This is an excellent opportunity to join a leading law firm and to use and develop experience in the legal property field.

title: Trade Mark Paralegal
description:
A highly regarded law firm is seeking an experienced Trade Mark Paralegal to join its busy Intellectual Property team.

This is an excellent opportunity for a Trade Mark Paralegal with at least 2 years' experience to support trade mark attorneys and lawyers across portfolio management, formalities and client matters within a collaborative and forward-thinking environment.

The Trade Mark Paralegal role:
- Managing and updating trade mark portfolios and databases
- Monitoring deadlines and maintaining accurate records
- Preparing and filing UKIPO and WIPO trade mark applications and forms
- Assisting with oppositions, cancellations and recordals
- Managing trade mark and domain name renewals
- Preparing client reports, cost estimates and invoices
- Liaising with clients, overseas attorneys and intellectual property offices
- Assisting with trade mark searches, watching services and portfolio audits
- Supporting global assignments and change of name recordals
- Assisting with evidence collection and general IP administration

The successful Trade Mark Paralegal:
- Minimum 2 years' Trade Mark Paralegal or IP administration experience
- Strong knowledge of trade mark formalities and portfolio management
- Excellent organisation and time management skills
- Exceptional attention to detail
- Experience using trade mark management databases
- WebTMS or IPPO experience would be advantageous
- Strong written and verbal communication skills
- Proactive, adaptable and able to work under pressure
- CITMA Paralegal Qualification would be advantageous

What's on offer:
- Salary of 26,000 - 30,000
- Opportunity to join a well-established IP team
- Direct exposure to trade mark attorneys and clients
- Supportive and collaborative working environment
- Ongoing training and development
- Clear opportunities for career progression

title: Up to mid-&;60s!! CIPA Patent Paralegal (12-month FTC)
company: Dawn Ellmore Employment Agency - Agency - Permanent
description:
We are working with a superb Law Firm in London who are seeking a bright and experienced CIPA Qualified Patent Paralegal to join their thriving team on a 12-month FTC. This is an exceptional opportunity to further your career within a well-established and outstanding Law Firm!

For this position, you must be CIPA Qualified and hold at least 2 years' experience as a Patent Paralegal or Patent Administrator and be able to seamlessly implement your knowledge into a busy role. You will be required to have excellent attention to detail as well as being able to time-manage and organise effectively.

Duties will include:
- Be in liaison with clients and Foreign Attorneys.
- Prepare and file patent applications.
- Provide support to other members of the team when needed.

Don't miss out on this incredible opportunity - get in touch now!

Dawn Ellmore Employment aims to respond to all applicants, however due to the number of applications received this is regrettably not always possible. If you have not received a response within three working days, you may assume that your application has been unsuccessful on this occasion.

title: Conveyancing Assistant
description:
Residential Conveyancing Assistant (Paralegal / Legal Secretary)
Permanent Office-Based

Salary

£25,000 - £30,000 per annum (dependent on experience)

About the Firm

An established and highly regarded regional law firm is seeking an experienced Residential Conveyancing Paralegal or Legal Secretary to join its busy and supportive property team.

The firm is known for its excellent client care, strong local reputation, and long-standing client relationships, including a steady flow of high-quality work from local agents and repeat clients. Staff retention is strong, and the firm genuinely invests in its people, offering a professional but friendly working environment where experience is valued and recognised.

This is a fully office-based role, ideal for someone who enjoys working closely with colleagues and being part of a collaborative team.

The Role

You will provide hands-on support to one or more fee earners handling a varied residential conveyancing caseload, including:
- Freehold and leasehold sales and purchases
- Re-mortgages
- Transfers of equity
- New build matters (where applicable)

The role would suit either an experienced paralegal or a skilled legal secretary with solid conveyancing exposure.

Key Responsibilities
- Supporting fee earners throughout the full conveyancing process
- Preparing and drafting standard conveyancing documentation
- Opening and closing files, carrying out AML and compliance checks
- Managing correspondence with clients, estate agents, solicitors, lenders and third parties
- Handling telephone and email enquiries professionally and confidently
- Using a case management system to progress matters efficiently
- Providing general administrative and secretarial support as required

About You
- Previous experience in residential conveyancing is essential
- Post completion knowledge
- Land registry experience
- Strong organisational skills and attention to detail
- Audio Dictation
- Confident communicator with a professional and client-focused approach
- Able to manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment
- Proficient in Microsoft Office and legal case management systems
- A positive, team-oriented attitude with a willingness to support others

What's on Offer
- Competitive salary of £25,000 - £30,000
- Stable, long-term permanent position
- Supportive and experienced conveyancing team
- Modern, well-run practice with a strong local reputation
- High-quality work and well-established processes
- Friendly, professional office environment

How to Apply

If you are an experienced Residential Conveyancing Paralegal or Legal Secretary looking for a secure role within a respected firm that values quality, teamwork and professionalism, this is an excellent opportunity.

Applications are welcomed from candidates seeking a long-term position within a stable and reputable practice.
